header: IN THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH AT KARACHI
(Umair Ahmed Siddiqui vs. Federation of Pakistan & others)
Date Order with Signature(s) of Judge(s)
1. FOR ORDERS ON OFFICE OBJECTIONS NO.1 AND 2
M/s. Aadil Channa, Syed Zaeem Hyder & Muzammil Ahmed,
Mr. Asim Iqbal, Advocate for Respondent/K-Electric along with
Syed Hyder Manager Corporate Litigation K-Electric, Ahmed
Javed, Manager, Legal K- Electric, Samad Wahab Kazi, Deputy
Ms. Wajiha Mehdi, Assistant Attorney General.
body: Ali Haider ‘Ada’ J.- The main contention of the petitioner in the instant petition is that respondent No.3, being the distribution company, disconnected the electricity supply to the petitioner’s premises without adopting the procedure prescribed under the relevant law. The petitioner alleges that respondent No.3 disconnected the electricity supply before expiry of the notice period, on the allegation of unauthorized extraction of load.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner had already lodged a complaint before the NEPRA Authority against the alleged illegal action of K-Electric. In this regard, the NEPRA Authority took cognizance of the matter, whereupon its Executive Office issued a notice dated 14.10.2026 to the concerned respondent. However, being aggrieved by the disconnection of electricity supply by K-Electric, the petitioner approached this Court by filing the instant constitutional petition.

3. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.3, while filing objections/comments on behalf of K-Electric, raised a preliminary objection regarding the maintainability of the petition. He further submitted that the petitioner, being a consumer, had violated the terms and conditions governing the sanctioned load by consuming electricity beyond the permissible limits. Despite repeated notices and an undertaking furnished by the petitioner to restrict consumption within the sanctioned load, the violation continued, compelling the respondent company to take action in accordance with law. He further contended that the circumstances reflect serious issues relating to load compliance and metering, and the petitioner cannot claim an unconditional right to continue receiving electricity beyond the sanctioned load. He further submits that, owing to the petitioner’s excessive consumption of electricity beyond the sanctioned load, the entire system was exposed to the risk of shutdown, as the additional load was being utilized without proper sanction, thereby causing substantial losses to respondent No.3.
4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.

5. So far as the alternate remedy already availed by the petitioner is concerned, it is evident that the matter is presently pending before the NEPRA Authority, which has also issued notice to K-Electric in respect of the grievance raised by the petitioner. In this regard, the Regulation of Generation, Transmission and Distribution of Electric Power Act, 1997, under Section 2(i), defines the Authority as the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA), while Section 3 provides for the establishment of the Authority, which is empowered to exercise its statutory functions under the Act. The competent authority is, therefore, required to examine the grievance raised by the petitioner and pass an appropriate order in accordance with the applicable legal framework.
6. Even otherwise, Section 24-A of the General Clauses Act, 1897, requires every public functionary to exercise its powers reasonably, fairly and justly, while recording reasons for its decisions.

7. In view of the foregoing circumstances, particularly when the matter is already seized by NEPRA and respondent No.3 has also been called upon to respond to the complaint, the competent authority of NEPRA is directed to decide the petitioner's grievance expeditiously, in accordance with law, through a reasoned and speaking order within a period of thirty days positively. In the meanwhile, the parties shall maintain the existing status quo regarding the supply of electricity, as directed through the earlier order of this Court, and the electricity supply to the petitioner's premises shall accordingly remain restored.

8. It is, however, clarified that any interim direction issued by this Court regarding restoration or continuation of electricity supply shall not influence the independent determination of the complaint by NEPRA. The competent authority shall examine the entire matter independently, taking into consideration the respective contentions of the parties, the material available on record and the applicable laws, rules and policies, and shall pass a well-reasoned order strictly in accordance with law.
9. Let a copy of this order be transmitted to the Director General, Consumer Affairs Department, NEPRA, Islamabad, for necessary action and compliance.
10. The instant petition stands disposed of in the above terms. JUDGE JUDGE
